sources.title: Adaptación y Resiliencia
sources.organization: Dirección de Cambio Climático, Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá
sources.temporal_coverage: Official page describing local adaptation projects and climate-adaptation water programming; project dates are not consistently stated.
sources.methodology: Official page text read; it summarizes ministry projects and objectives.
sources.limitations: Undated page mixes completed activities with expected outputs; no impact evaluation.

sources.title: Programa de Adaptación al Cambio Climático a través del Manejo Integrado de los Recursos Hídricos presenta resultados impactantes en cuencas priorizadas
sources.organization: Dirección de Cambio Climático, Ministerio de Ambiente de Panamá
sources.methodology: MiAmbiente summary of two watershed projects.
sources.limitations: Implementer-reported; no evaluation or basin-specific beneficiary split.

sources.title: Panama: National Case Study
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical drought record and social/service indicators with vintages mainly from 2013 and 2021–2023.
sources.methodology: FAO drought-portal country profile presents selected hazard pathways and social, economic and infrastructure indicators.
sources.limitations: Underlying datasets and methods are not detailed on this profile; indicator years differ and are not current estimates.

sources.title: Agua y el Canal
sources.temporal_coverage: Live water-management page with 2023 drought facts and planning information current at October 2026 access.
sources.methodology: Canal Authority page describes water operations, service areas and water-project planning.
sources.limitations: Institutional account, not independent assessment; dated facts and live-page material are distinguished.

sources.title: Parlamentarios británicos visitan la comunidad de Gardi Sugdub en la comarca Guna Yala
sources.temporal_coverage: Official account of a January 2024 visit and then-planned relocation to Isberyala.
sources.methodology: Ministry press account of a site visit and discussion with Guna Congress participants and Sáhilas.
sources.limitations: Dated event report, not a household survey or follow-up on completion, consent or service delivery.

sources.title: Fenómeno de El Niño – SINAPROC
sources.organization: Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil, Panamá
sources.temporal_coverage: 2026 El Niño alert, emergency declaration and July–December 2026 outlook as stated on the live page.
sources.methodology: Civil-protection page summarizes official meteorological and hydrological monitoring and response arrangements.
sources.limitations: Forecast lacks model/scenario details; response descriptions are not evaluation results.

claims.locator: Section ‘Fortalecimiento de capacidades a municipios vulnerables’; paragraphs beginning ‘Descripción’ and ‘Actualmente se ha desarrollado la metodología’.
claims.paraphrase: MiAmbiente reports a vulnerability-index method and two capacity workshops completed with the initially selected municipalities, including Las Palmas (Veraguas) and Chame (Panamá Oeste); maps are intended to distinguish corregimientos and inform local planning.
claims.limitations: The undated page mixes completed workshops with maps and risk assessments described as planned outputs.

claims.paraphrase: The ministry describes a Kusapín, Ngäbe-Buglé pilot involving local, government and traditional authorities and proposing gender-aware vulnerability mapping, participatory land-use planning, climate-risk management and local planner training.
claims.limitations: The page lists project objectives and intended outputs; it does not establish that all maps or plans were completed.

claims.locator: Water-programme section, paragraphs beginning ‘Para hacer esto’ and ‘En paralelo’.
claims.paraphrase: The programme says climate-informed water-right decisions aim to strengthen governance in two basins selected partly due to existing water-user conflicts.
claims.limitations: Conflicts are context; climate change is not stated to cause or escalate them.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Climate-informed allocation aims to improve governance where user conflicts already exist; climate change is not stated to cause them.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Same water-programme section, paragraph beginning ‘En paralelo’, and preceding paragraph naming unresolved water-user conflicts.

claims.locator: Opening results paragraphs beginning ‘El programa…’ and ‘Panamá cuenta…’.
claims.paraphrase: MiAmbiente reports over 116,000 direct and indirect beneficiaries across the climate-vulnerable Chiriquí Viejo and Santa María basins; consultations raised crop-loss, extreme-event and drinking-water quantity and quality concerns.
claims.limitations: The total combines direct and indirect beneficiaries without a basin split; consultation concerns are not prevalence estimates.

claims.locator: Results obtained, Result 1, paragraph beginning ‘El programa implementó’.
claims.paraphrase: The ministry reports adaptation practices on 120 farms covering 600 hectares of silvopastoral systems, 226 hectares of agroforestry and 50 rainwater-harvesting systems, including in Santa María basin.
claims.limitations: Implementer-reported outputs; farm and hectare totals are not divided between the two basins.

claims.locator: Results obtained, Result 2, paragraphs beginning ‘El programa desarrolló’ and ‘Se elaboró’.
claims.paraphrase: The programme reports eight climate-resilient water-management instruments, including vulnerability studies, adaptation plans, hydrological balances and environmental flows, plus soil-climate zoning for 12 priority crops.
claims.limitations: The account lists completed technical outputs but does not evaluate their effects on allocation decisions.

claims.locator: Results obtained, Result 3, paragraphs beginning ‘Se fortaleció’ and ‘Se implementaron’.
claims.paraphrase: The programme reports over 40 agrometeorological and hydrological stations, two flood early-warning systems in priority basins and advice for over 6,000 producers across five regions.
claims.limitations: The producer figure is programme-wide across five regions, not per-region; reported outputs are not independently evaluated.

claims.paraphrase: FAO names Arco Seco, Veraguense savanna, Cerro Punta and Ngäbe-Buglé as drought-affected; 2019 was severe and 2023–24 rainfall was 43% below average.
claims.limitations: The 43% figure concerns the 2023–24 episode, not each named zone.

claims.paraphrase: FAO says drought threatens subsistence farmers’ food security and drinking/sanitation water, while low Canal levels disrupt maritime operations and revenue.
claims.limitations: National pathway summary; no household counts or specific climate-change attribution.

claims.locator: Social indicators, bullets on rural poverty and Indigenous comarcas.
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports rural poverty at 29.3% (2022) and 32.3% (2023); 76% of Indigenous people live rurally, and three Indigenous comarcas had the highest 2021 poverty indicators.
institutions: national statistical sources cited by FAO
claims.limitations: Different vintages; contextual indicators, not drought-caused poverty estimates.

claims.locator: Infrastructural indicators, bullets on rural water and sanitation.
claims.paraphrase: In 2022, basic water access was 86.1% rural versus 94.6% nationally; sanitation was 66.4% versus 85.9%.
institutions: national statistical sources cited by FAO
claims.limitations: Not comarca-specific or a measure of drought impacts.

claims.locator: Water page paragraph beginning ‘Vale la pena recordar que 2023’.
claims.paraphrase: The Canal Authority says 2023 was the third-driest year in the Canal basin, with about 30% rainfall deficit; it cut daily transits from July because it could not store over half the water needed for the 2024 dry season.
claims.limitations: Historical 2023–24 account from the operator, not a current restriction or climate-attribution analysis.

claims.locator: Water page paragraphs beginning ‘Frente a los desafíos’ and ‘En la Cuenca del Canal’.
claims.paraphrase: The Authority says Canal reservoirs supply water to over half of Panama’s population, including Panama City, San Miguelito, Arraiján, La Chorrera and Colón, and support Canal operations and other economic uses.
affected_groups: more than half of national population
claims.limitations: The page gives a system-wide service share, not district proportions or a current shortage count.

claims.locator: Water page paragraphs beginning ‘Asimismo, se mantienen las medidas’ and ‘Al mismo tiempo, avanza’.
claims.paraphrase: The Authority says water-saving measures adopted in December 2025 remain for the 2026 dry season; the proposed Río Indio lake is a long-term project requiring community participation and respect for residents’ rights.
claims.limitations: Savings are reported as ongoing; Río Indio is planning, not a completed infrastructure or relocation outcome.

claims.locator: Main text paragraphs beginning ‘En los últimos meses’ and ‘MiAMBIENTE destaca’.
claims.paraphrase: MiAmbiente linked sea-level rise at Gardi Sugdub, Guna Yala, to an impending mainland relocation to Isberyala and called it climate displacement; its January 2024 report does not document completion.
claims.limitations: Dated 2024 account of a planned process; it does not quantify hazard or households or evaluate voluntariness or completion.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: MiAmbiente explicitly calls the planned Gardi Sugdub relocation climate displacement and links it to sea-level rise; it does not associate the process with conflict or violence.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Main text paragraphs beginning ‘En los últimos meses’ and ‘MiAMBIENTE destaca’.

claims.locator: Main text paragraph beginning ‘El Grupo Interparlamentario Británico participó’.
claims.paraphrase: At a January 2024 Guna Congress meeting, Sáhilas described basic needs for new Isberyala, including water, health services and household furniture.
claims.limitations: The report records needs raised at one meeting; it does not establish which remained unmet after relocation.

claims.locator: Page paragraphs beginning ‘El 26 de agosto de 2026’ and ‘El Sistema Nacional de Protección Civil’.
claims.paraphrase: Government declared a national emergency on 26 August 2026 for El Niño-related conditions after a May alert; SINAPROC describes monitoring, interagency coordination and public-preparedness functions.
affected_groups: communities exposed to drought and heavy rain
claims.limitations: Declaration and described arrangements show response capacity, not effectiveness or aid distribution.

claims.locator: Page paragraphs beginning ‘De acuerdo con la información presentada’ and ‘No obstante’.
claims.paraphrase: SINAPROC reports forecast predominant rainfall deficits nationwide from July through December 2026, potentially reaching 55% in some zones, while noting contrasting rainfall and flood risks on the Caribbean slope.
claims.scenario: Official July–December 2026 rainfall outlook cites deficits up to 55% in some zones; forecast model and scenario are not stated.
claims.limitations: Contemporaneous official forecast, not observed outcome; maximum-deficit zones are not named.

claims.locator: Page paragraphs beginning ‘Actualmente, el IMHPA reporta’ and ‘En contraste’.
claims.paraphrase: The page reports 11 hydrographic basins currently under water stress and unusually high rainfall in parts of Bocas del Toro, with flood, river-rise and landslide conditions possible in vulnerable areas.
affected_groups: communities in vulnerable areas of Bocas del Toro
claims.limitations: The page does not name the 11 basins or quantify population and asset exposure in Bocas del Toro.

search_audit.query: Panama climate vulnerability drought indigenous comarcas Chiriquí Viejo Santa María basin report government FAO
search_audit.outcome: Read official watershed-programme material and FAO profile; FAO names drought zones but uses heterogeneous indicator vintages.

search_audit.query: Panama climate conflict water user conflict displacement indigenous climate security report official
search_audit.outcome: Official programme reports existing water-user conflicts in two basins and MiAmbiente frames Gardi Sugdub relocation as climate displacement; no climate-caused violence finding verified.

search_audit.query: Panama conflict insecurity land tenure adaptation constraints climate resilience indigenous comarca report UNDP
search_audit.outcome: No source-verified claim found that conflict or insecurity constrained climate adaptation; Guna relocation report records service needs but does not assess tenure, consent or conflict.

search_audit.query: Panama local climate adaptation resilience water communities Canal indigenous official government project report
search_audit.outcome: Read local municipal and Indigenous-comarca planning, watershed programme results, Canal water planning and 2026 civil-protection response/forecast information.

gaps: No directly read public source in this extraction established climate change causing or worsening violent conflict in Panama; reported water-user conflicts are contextual to adaptation programming.
The official 2026 climate-mobility report exceeded fetch limits and the 2024 NDC2 PDF open timed out; indexed snippets were not used.
MiAmbiente's January 2024 Gardi Sugdub account records impending relocation and service needs but not subsequent completion, consent, tenure outcomes or service quality.
FAO rural-service and poverty indicators use different vintages from 2021–2023 and do not provide consistent district/comarca-level drought impact estimates.
